=== CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===
- scripts/gh_helpers.sh:1274-1358 | severity=high | confidence=5
  flagged_by: [mistralai_mistral-small-2603, moonshotai_kimi-k2_5, x-ai_grok-4_20]
  PROBLEM: The helper returns 0 on probe failures, so the caller treats an inconclusive budget probe as “budget consumed” and skips the changes-lost retry path.
  WHY: A transient GitHub API flake, malformed response, or jq failure can permanently suppress the only automated retry for that head SHA and recreate the original stall-recovery dead end.
- scripts/gh_helpers.sh:1334-1344 | severity=high | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [mistralai_mistral-small-2603, moonshotai_kimi-k2_5]
  PROBLEM: The jq filter can treat an API error envelope or missing `.workflow_runs` payload as an empty run list instead of a failed probe.
  WHY: If GitHub returns an error body that still reaches the parser, the helper can conclude “no prior runs” and allow a retry when the budget check was actually inconclusive.
- .github/workflows/review_autofix.yml:6242-6260 | severity=high | confidence=5
  flagged_by: [mistralai_mistral-small-2603]
  PROBLEM: The re-dispatch step uses `env.PR_NUMBER != ''` but does not explicitly declare `PR_NUMBER` in the step-level environment, so the guard can resolve empty and block the re-dispatch.
  WHY: If `PR_NUMBER` is not available to that step, the changes-lost recovery never fires and the original dead-end remains reachable.
- .github/workflows/review_autofix.yml:6296-6299 | severity=high | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [mistralai_mistral-small-2603, moonshotai_kimi-k2_5, x-ai_grok-4_20]
  PROBLEM: `TARGET_BRANCH` is passed into the budget helper without validation that it is non-empty.
  WHY: If the checkout step early-aborts or `TARGET_BRANCH` is empty, the helper can probe the wrong branch or an empty branch filter, suppressing a valid retry.
- scripts/gh_helpers.sh:1308-1321 | severity=high | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro, mistralai_mistral-small-2603, moonshotai_kimi-k2_5]
  PROBLEM: The budget probe only inspects the first 30 runs, so older completed runs on the same head SHA can be missed on busy branches.
  WHY: Pagination can make the budget appear available when it is already consumed, allowing extra automated retries on the same head SHA.
- scripts/gh_helpers.sh:1334-1344 | severity=high | confidence=5
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro, mistralai_mistral-small-2603, x-ai_grok-4_20]
  PROBLEM: The workflow-name regex hard-codes the current review-family YAML filenames, so new variants are invisible to the budget check.
  WHY: Runs from an unrecognized review workflow filename would not count against the head SHA retry budget, defeating the one-retry-per-head contract.
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:12382-12431 | severity=high | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [mistralai_mistral-small-2603, x-ai_grok-4_20]
  PROBLEM: `extract_recommended_answers()` only processes the most recent clarification comment, so later comments can hide earlier recommended answers.
  WHY: Intended answers can be lost when the thread grows before the parser runs, preventing auto-answer and recreating the stall.
- scripts/gh_helpers.sh:1253-1358 | severity=low | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [x-ai_grok-4_20]
  PROBLEM: The new helper has no entry in `docs/scripts-pending-removal.md`.
  WHY: The reviewer flagged this as a §20.F registry-contract gap for the added operational helper.

=== FINDINGS FROM deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro ===
- File: scripts/gh_helpers.sh
  Line or code reference: 1308-1311 (the `gh_retry gh api ... 2>/dev/null` call)
  Problem: The `gh api` call in `autofix_changes_lost_head_retry_consumed` uses `-f "per_page=30"`. The GitHub Actions runs endpoint returns results in descending order by run ID. If the PR head branch accumulates more than 30 review-family workflow runs, a prior completed run on the same head SHA could fall past the first page and be invisible to the budget check, making the budget incorrectly appear available.
  Why it fails at runtime: A busy orchestrator integration branch can accumulate many review runs from sub-issue PR merges. If the relevant prior completed run is pushed past page 1 by newer runs, the budget check returns "budget available" when it is actually consumed, allowing an extra dispatch.
  SEVERITY: NIT
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 2

- File: scripts/gh_helpers.sh
  Line or code reference: 1340 (the jq filter path regex)
  Problem: The jq filter in `autofix_changes_lost_head_retry_consumed` matches review-family workflows with the hardcoded regex `(^|/)(review_autofix|internal-review|ai-review)\\.ya?ml$`. If a new review workflow variant is added under a different filename (for example `ai-review-v2.yml`), runs from that workflow would be invisible to the budget check, silently bypassing the one-retry-per-head contract.
  Why it fails at runtime: A completed run from an unrecognized review workflow filename would not be counted as consuming the head SHA's retry budget, defeating the loop guard for any head reviewed by the new variant.
  SEVERITY: NIT
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 2
=== END FINDINGS FROM deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro ===

=== FINDINGS FROM mistralai_mistral-small-2603 ===
- File: scripts/gh_helpers.sh
  Code: autofix_changes_lost_head_retry_consumed function return on probe failures
  Problem: The helper returns 0 (budget consumed) on any probe failure (API error, jq error, empty response, missing inputs), causing the caller to skip the changes-lost retry path. This makes transient failures permanently suppress the retry for that head SHA.
  Why it fails at runtime: The retry dispatch treats 0 as "budget consumed," so a GitHub API flake or malformed response can silently block the only automated retry, recreating the original stall-recovery dead end.
  SEVERITY: MAJOR
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 5

- File: .github/workflows/review_autofix.yml
  Code: Re-dispatch step guard using env.PR_NUMBER
  Problem: The re-dispatch step uses `env.PR_NUMBER != ''` but does not explicitly declare `PR_NUMBER` in the step-level environment, so it can resolve empty and block the re-dispatch, recreating the original dead-end.
  Why it fails at runtime: If `PR_NUMBER` is not explicitly passed into the step environment, the guard evaluates false and the changes-lost recovery never fires.
  SEVERITY: MAJOR
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 5

- File: scripts/gh_helpers.sh
  Code: per_page=30 limit in gh api call
  Problem: The budget probe only inspects 30 runs, but review-family runs are returned in descending order by run_id. On busy branches with >30 review runs on the same head branch, older completed runs on the same head SHA can be missed, causing the budget to appear available when it's already consumed.
  Why it fails at runtime: The one-retry-per-head accounting can be defeated by pagination, allowing multiple automated retries on the same head SHA.
  SEVERITY: MAJOR
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 4

- File: scripts/gh_helpers.sh
  Code: jq filter handling of error JSON envelopes
  Problem: The jq filter uses `.workflow_runs[]?` and treats a 200 response with an error JSON envelope as an empty run list instead of a failed probe. This can produce a false-negative budget check, allowing a retry when the API actually signaled an error.
  Why it fails at runtime: Transient GitHub API errors or auth failures that return HTTP 200 with an error body would be treated as "no prior runs" rather than "probe failed," defeating the fail-closed intent.
  SEVERITY: MAJOR
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 4

- File: scripts/gh_helpers.sh
  Code: workflow path regex in budget probe
  Problem: The jq filter hard-codes `(^|/)(review_autofix|internal-review|ai-review)\.ya?ml$`, so runs from newer review workflow variants (e.g., ai-review-v2.yml) are invisible to the budget check, defeating the "one automated retry per head" contract.
  Why it fails at runtime: The budget accounting can be bypassed by unrecognized workflow filenames, allowing multiple automated retries on the same head SHA.
  SEVERITY: MAJOR
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 5

- File: scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh
  Code: extract_recommended_answers() only processes the most recent clarification comment
  Problem: The perl one-liner extracts recommended answers from only the latest clarification comment, so later comments can hide the earlier recommended answers. In the stall-recovery case, the intended answers can be lost when the comment thread grows before the parser runs.
  Why it fails at runtime: Recommended answers for original questions can be silently discarded, preventing auto-answer and recreating the original stall.
  SEVERITY: MAJOR
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 4

- Requirement: "The per-head-SHA budget deliberately keeps the original single-shot intent of the removed event-payload guard: at most one automated changes-lost retry per head"
  Expected change site: .github/workflows/review_autofix.yml or scripts/gh_helpers.sh
  Evidence of absence: No test coverage for the scenario where TARGET_BRANCH env variable is undefined or empty when autofix_changes_lost_head_retry_consumed is called. The helper requires head_branch but there's no validation that TARGET_BRANCH is set before the call site.
  SEVERITY: MAJOR
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 4

- Requirement: "clarification comments are matched by their <!-- ai:clarification-questions --> body marker alone (also fixes plan.yml's stale-clarification cleanup)"
  Expected change site: scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh extract_recommended_answers() and the corresponding plan.yml jq block
  Evidence of absence: The perl one-liner was updated, but the comment in plan.yml still says "Find clarification comments by HTML marker or legacy..." and the jq still only cleans stale clarification comments on the same issue. The PR never updated the stale-cleanup path to also use the body-marker-only rule.
  SEVERITY: MAJOR
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 4

- Requirement: "New/extended tests: tests/test_plan_auto_answer_recommended_parser.py (43 pass...)"
  Expected change site: tests/test_plan_auto_answer_recommended_parser.py (the new test_extract_recommended_answers_* helpers)
